title: What Happens When Insurance Expires? Renewals, Terms, and Next Steps
description: Learn what happens when term life, auto, and home insurance policies reach their expiration dates: automatic renewals, non-renewal notices, conversion privileges, and gap management.
author: Sophia Lin

content.text: What occurs when an [insurance policy](/learn/what-is-an-insurance-policy) reaches its expiration date depends entirely on whether the policy is an annual renewable property contract or a fixed-duration life contract.
1. Auto and Home Insurance Expiration (Annual Policies)
Most auto and homeowner policies are issued for 6 or 12 month terms. In the vast majority of cases, they renew automatically:

items: Automatic Renewal: 30 to 45 days before expiration, the carrier mails an updated Declarations Page with the new term's premium. If your payments are on autopay, coverage continues uninterrupted.

Non-Renewal Notice: If the carrier decides not to renew your policy (e.g., due to multiple at-fault claims or withdrawal from your geographic market), state law requires 30 to 60 days advance written notice so you can shop for replacement coverage, as regulated by the [NAIC](https://content.naic.org/).

content.text: 2. What Happens When a Term Life Policy Expires?
When a 20- or 30-year [term life insurance policy](/learn/term-insurance-guide) reaches the end of its level-premium period, you have three primary options:

rows: Simply allow the policy to terminate if your children are grown, mortgage is paid, and you no longer need income protection.
Keep the existing policy active on a year-by-year basis without taking a medical exam.
Premiums increase dramatically (often 5x to 10x higher per year) based on your attained age.
Convert your term policy into a permanent whole life policy with zero medical underwriting before reaching age 65 or 70.
Locks in permanent coverage at whole life premium rates.

content.title: The Conversion Privilege Advantage
content.text: If you develop serious medical conditions (heart disease, cancer) during your term, the conversion option is invaluable: it guarantees you can secure permanent life coverage that would otherwise be impossible to buy on the open market.

items.question: Is there a grace period after my policy expires?
items.answer: No. Once a fixed term officially expires without renewal, coverage terminates immediately at 12:01 AM on the expiration date.

content.text: Conversion terms and deadlines vary by life insurer. Check your policy contract.
